newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-UKRAINE SCRAPE TO 1-0 WIN OVER ALBANIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UKRAINE SCRAPE TO 1-0 WIN OVER ALBANIA.

text.p: Ukraine kept the pressure on Portugal and Germany in world cup qualifying group nine with a narrow 1-0 win over Albania in neutral Granada on Saturday.

Ukraine's victory -- courtesy of a 39th minute goal from Serguei Rebrov -- lifted them to nine points, the same total as group leaders Portugal who drew 0-0 with Northern Ireland earlier in the day. In Ukraine's favour is the fact Portugal have played two more matches.
European champions Germany, currently in third spot in the group but the favourites to secure the one automatic berth for the finals in France next year, did not play.

Albanian goalkeeper Foto Strakosha came close to giving his strife-torn country an unexpected boost after turning in a superb performance but in the end Albania were left looking for their first win in the group after three defeats and a draw.
The game was moved to Spain because of the political unrest in the Balkan country but only 250 spectators paid to see what turned out to be a closely-fought affair.

Albania came close to securing what would have been a surprise draw 12 minutes from the end but wasted a clearcut chance when substitute Alban Bujhaj missed with a header after outjumping the Ukranian defence at a corner.
Despite that, coach Haafizi Astrit was clearly happy with the way his side played, especially his goalkeeper who made a series of fine saves.
"The Albanian people love and enjoy football, even in a difficult situation like now," he said.
Astrit's men had the first clear chance after 20 minutes when Artan Bellai put Bledar Kola through but his shot brushed the post with the Ukraine keeper beaten.
Shortly after that Albania had the ball in the net when Altin Rrakill kept his head to knock in a loose ball, only to see the goal disallowed for offside.
Ukraine took control from then on, going ahead just before half-time when Andriy Shevchenko advanced down the right before finding Rebrov, who had no problem beating goalkeeper Foto Strakosha.
Ukranian captain Youri Kalitvintsev could have put his side further ahead straight from the restart after the break with a fine shot from just outside the area that went narrowly wide.
